name: Thiers-Issard razors

card.summary: Straight razors from the French maker Thiers-Issard, used for traditional blade shaving that gives a close, clean-shaven face.
card.note: Straight razors require technique and maintenance; beginners are commonly advised toward round points.

quick.overview:
Thiers-Issard is a French maker of straight razors, listed by Wikipedia among Europe's best-known. Its razors are folding blades with a handle, used for wet shaving to leave the face smooth.

The appearance payoff is a close, clean shave for people who prefer it to cartridges or electrics. Forum users on T Nation have recommended the brand in threads about shaving.
quick.how: The blade is held at roughly 30 degrees and moved across the skin; the edge is kept aligned by stropping on leather and restored by honing on whetstones. Carbon steel is easier to hone but rusts more readily than stainless.
quick.risks: An open blade can cut skin, and square or spike points can nick inexperienced users. Very thin hollow-ground blades flex and are unsuited to heavy beard growth. Some jurisdictions require barbers to use disposable-blade shavettes for hygiene.

lead: Thiers-Issard is a French straight razor maker. Wikipedia calls it one of Europe's best-known razor makers, noting that French makers such as Thiers Issard still use Sheffield silver steel and that it is noted for decorated blades and Damascus steel [1].

People use straight razors as a traditional route to a close shave. Interest in them revived after the 2012 film Skyfall featured a straight razor shave, according to Wikipedia [1]. On the bodybuilding forum T Nation, posters in 2008 and 2009 shaving threads named the brand, with one writing that nothing comes close to it [2][3].

chain: Shave with a honed, stropped straight razor
Blade cuts hair close to the skin
angle.text: A well-kept straight razor produces a close shave, and users value it as a premium alternative to cartridge razors.

infobox: Decorated blades, Damascus steel, Sheffield silver steel

paras: Straight razors have scales that protect the blade when folded and protect the user from accidental cuts. Blade width and point shape affect handling, and round points are recommended for beginners [4].
Stropping on leather keeps the edge aligned, while honing on whetstones restores sharpness. Carbon steel is easier to hone but rusts more readily; stainless resists rust but is harder to hone [4].
In T Nation threads, one poster wrote that a Thiers Issard straight razor was the best, another listed owning one among underrated pleasures, and a third named it alongside Dovo [2][3][5].
Square or spike points can nick inexperienced users, and thin hollow-ground blades suit light beards [4].
